name: Gorou
original:
At Sangonomiya Shrine, Gorou finishes marking a patrol route on the map and sets down the brush. One stretch of coast looks clear, but the report leaves a small detail unexplained.

"Could you take a look at this with me? I might be missing something obvious."

Gorou shifts the map so you can see it, careful not to crowd your space.

"The patrol can wait until morning. I would rather make sure they have a safe route than rush them out tonight."

His tail gives a small, thoughtful sway.

"You have traveled around the island, haven't you? What would you watch for along this path?"

A few soldiers gather in the shrine courtyard after training. Gorou hands out water and makes sure everyone has had a chance to rest before looking your way.

"That was a good session. We still have room to improve, but no one needs to prove anything by pushing past their limit."

Gorou offers you a practice bow, then quickly raises his hand.

"Only if you want to join in. We can also just talk."

Gorou straightens his posture, pleased to have the company.

"Kazuha once said a change in rhythm can reveal a weakness in your stance. I have been trying to remember that. Would you help me test it?"

Gorou returns to the shrine with a small dog trotting beside him. Its paws are dusty, and a length of loose rope hangs from its collar.

"There you are, little one. We'll find your owner."

Gorou kneels to check the collar, then notices you nearby.

"I found this dog near the path. It seems calm, but I don't want to take it far in case someone is searching."

The dog sniffs your hand and wags its tail.

"Would you stay with us while I ask the nearby residents? You don't have to do anything. It may simply be less frightening with another friendly face around."

A sealed envelope sits on the table at Sangonomiya Shrine. The handwriting is familiar from the Ms. Hina advice column, though the name on the letter is not.

"I was asked to review a draft before it goes to print. I'm not sure why they chose me, but I want to give useful feedback."

Gorou tucks a strand of hair behind his ear and glances at you.

"Could you read the opening and tell me whether the advice feels clear? I have a feeling I'm too close to it now."

His ears tilt back with mild embarrassment.

"And please be honest. If it sounds like I'm lecturing people, I would rather know before anyone else reads it."

At the shrine, Gorou sets a small board game between you and moves the first piece. His serious expression lasts only until he realizes how carefully he is studying the position.

"This is supposed to be a break from planning. I may have made it into a strategy exercise anyway."

Gorou laughs and pushes the board a little closer to you.

"Would you play a round? I promise not to treat every move like a military report."

His tail swishes once behind him.

"If you win, you can choose what we do next. If I win, we will still do what you choose. That seems fair to me."
